long_biography.plain_text:
CVC's 1993 management buyout turned Citicorp Venture Capital's European operation into an independent private-equity firm, with Rolly van Rappard among the co-founders. He had joined the predecessor business after working for Citicorp in corporate finance in London and Amsterdam. Van Rappard went on to chair CVC's regional private-equity boards, which oversaw day-to-day management of its investment businesses.

Educated in law at Utrecht and economics at Columbia, van Rappard moved from deal leadership into founder stewardship. He became co-chair in 2013 and now chairs the listed company's board and nomination committee. His continuing position preserves a role in CVC's governance while its chief executive and senior management run daily operations.

uncertainties.detail: CVC uses Rolly van Rappard professionally. Official filings give Louis Rodolph Jules Ridder van Rappard, while the Hoge Raad van Adel states that ridder is a lower-case noble title placed between given names and family name. The dossier therefore proposes Louis Rodolph Jules ridder van Rappard as the display form and Rodolph Jules as the middle names; it does not treat ridder as a middle name or wealth signal.

The source site's generic title field may render before the first name, whereas Dutch official styling places ridder between the given names and family name. The title field remains unproposed, with ridder retained as an 80-confidence mapping candidate pending confirmation of the site's rendering behaviour.

Official records give Curaçao as the birthplace. In 1960 it formed part of the Netherlands Antilles and it is now a constituent country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands. The dossier proposes Curaçao only for place_of_birth and leaves the existing birth-country select value unchanged because its historical-versus-current country convention and available option label were not established.

CVC's reported assets under management represent fund and client capital managed by the firm, not van Rappard's personal wealth. The classifications rely instead on his disclosed founder shares and separately reported family-office interests.

CVC funds hold interests in operating companies, but the companies' assets, workforce and enterprise values remain corporate property. Van Rappard's CVC role and shareholding do not make those underlying operating assets his direct personal property.
